solution: In the 1980s section the chapter says of Rajiv Gandhi: "He took the lead in solving the issues of the Tamil minority in Sri Lanka. He promoted the idea of a united Sri Lanka with internal autonomy to the Tamil community, but his efforts in this regard proved to be in vain." Indira Gandhi, Devegowda and Narasimha Rao are discussed in the chapter for other things (Emergency/Bangladesh, coalition-era premiership, economic liberalisation) and none is linked to the Sri Lankan Tamil issue.

The Science and technology section states: "Dr M. S. Swaminathan is known as the father of the Green Revolution in 1965. He implemented new scientific agricultural techniques and increased the production of foodgrains." Verghese Kurien is credited in the very next sentences with the co-operative dairy movement (White Revolution) and Homi Bhabha with the atomic power programme; Norman Borlaug is not mentioned in the chapter (he is the father of the Green Revolution globally, but the stem asks specifically about India).
